title: Today was a good day for Argus.
author: Zephyr_Labs
selftext:
I’ve been building an experimental market-research and paper-trading system called Argus, and today was the first day it ran a real prospective session under frozen rules.  
And it went **5 for fucking 6**.  
Not five cherry-picked historical examples. Six actual paper trades triggered during the live market from patterns that had already been discovered, tested, qualified, and frozen before the session started.  
Today’s trades:  
Trade 1 short: **-0.835%**  
Trade 2 long: **+1.045%**  
Trade 3 short: **+1.844%**  
Trade 4: **+0.278%**  
Trade 5: **+0.099%**  
Trade 6 long: **+0.033%**  
That’s **5 winners out of 6 trades**, an **83.3% directional win rate**, and about **+1.21% gross portfolio growth** on a roughly $2,000 paper account.  
No real money was involved. This is still an experiment.  
But this was the part I’ve been trying to get to for weeks.  
Argus did not wake up this morning and optimize itself around today’s market. The patterns were frozen before trading started. During the session it watched completed market bars, detected when those existing patterns fired, applied the existing qualification gates, ranked the candidates, entered using an observed post-signal market price, managed the position, and exited based on the existing stop or 30-minute horizon.  
The full chain finally worked:  
historical discovery  
→ holdout validation  
→ freeze the qualified pattern  
→ live signal detection  
→ qualification  
→ paper entry  
→ position management  
→ exit  
→ recorded P&L  
And on the first day that entire prospective loop actually ran, **five of the six trades moved the direction Argus predicted.**  
The one loser was a stopped short at about -0.84%.  
Then later in the morning the exact same pattern fired again, Argus took the short again, and that one returned about **+1.84%**.  
That was probably my favorite trade of the day because the system didn’t get emotional about being wrong the first time. It just evaluated the next signal under the same rules and took it.  
There were engineering problems. The controller hung twice late in the session while managing a position and had to be restarted. The good news is the trade state persisted correctly, including the original entry and timing, and the final trade still closed at its intended horizon.  
So runtime reliability still needs work.  
There’s also an old fixed transaction-cost rule in the accounting layer that I’m removing. It currently applies arbitrary cost assumptions to each trade and turns some tiny winners into accounting losses. Until I replace that with defensible spread/slippage measurements, I’m treating **+1.21% gross** as the meaningful number and real executable net as unknown.  
But none of that changes the thing I’m excited about:  
**The system made six prospective decisions today. Five were right.**  
That does not prove a profitable strategy. Six trades is nowhere near enough data for that.  
But six trades is enough to prove something I genuinely wasn’t sure I could build:  
A pattern-discovery system can find behavior historically, freeze it, recognize it again in a market it hasn’t seen yet, and make the correct directional call **5 times out of 6 on day one**.  
Now I get to find out whether today was luck or the beginning of an actual edge.  
And for once, I’m extremely happy to have that problem.
